component_records.title: Project management, governance and weekly reporting
component_records.description: A dedicated project manager and named technical staff are assigned from award, with a personnel management plan identifying roles, availability and escalation paths (R106). The team holds weekly meetings with City Accounting and IT to monitor progress, budget and timeline against a milestone plan, with written status, issue log and change control (R105). The plan is built backwards from a July 1, 2026 go-live so that configuration, migration, parallel running and training all complete before the City's fiscal year opens (R067). A client engagement approach with a named account manager covers the full contract term, and the implementation schedule and task sequence are submitted with the fee proposal (R120).

component_records.title: Hosted cloud accounting and financial reporting platform
component_records.description: A multi-module cloud system is provided on a hosted subscription basis, covering Accounts Payable with 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approval routing, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing (R008). Transactions post systematically through the general ledger with budgeting and forecasting built into the same data model, so budget-to-actual and multi-year projections come from live postings rather than spreadsheets (R004). Reporting and analytics include standard financial statements, ad-hoc query and export, and dashboard views for management decision-making (R005). Every posting carries user, date and approval audit trail, and records are retained and retrievable for audit and future reference (R006). The system is delivered as acquisition plus implementation, with the City owning its data and configuration (R002).

component_records.title: Account structure design and auditable reporting
component_records.description: Before configuration, the team reviews the City's current chart of accounts and recommends a fund, department, function and object structure that supports auditable reporting and clean fund accounting (R108). The recommendation is documented with a mapping from old to new account codes and is reviewed with the City's auditors' expectations in mind, demonstrating the vendor's understanding of the auditing and reporting requirements that apply to a California city's financial statements (R107). Financial report writing is delivered as a hands-on workstream: the vendor builds the City's core statements and budget reports with City staff, then trains staff to maintain and modify them (R109). Account number customization — segment lengths, code formats, and the ability to add or restructure segments without re-implementation — is described in the proposal so the City can confirm flexibility for future funds and grants (R062).

component_records.title: Data migration of five years of history
component_records.description: The vendor extracts, maps, cleans and loads the prior five years of financial, payroll, utility billing and licensing history from the City's existing Tyler Fund Balance system into the new platform, with reconciliation reports proving opening balances and historical detail tie out (R110). Migration runs in a test environment first, with City Accounting validating trial balances and key reports before the production cutover. Cutover is scheduled over a weekend and outside billing cycles, with parallel running where practical, to reduce downtime and operational impact during the transition (R112). The migration plan is executed jointly with City Accounting and IT, with named counterparts, a data-cleansing responsibility matrix and a rollback plan agreed before cutover (R111).

component_records.title: Training and change management
component_records.description: Power users in Accounting receive personalized, role-based training on configuration, period close, report writing and utility billing and licensing workflows, with a written manual tailored to the City's own account structure (R113). All staff receive at least one recorded training session plus a general user manual, retained for onboarding future employees (R115). Training is offered in person, virtual and recorded formats by license level, so the City can choose the mix that fits its small staff (R071). Training is scheduled before go-live with refresher sessions after the first close, and completion is tracked in the project plan.

component_records.title: Ongoing support, help desk and annual e-filing
component_records.description: A ticketing help desk is provided from go-live, with defined priority levels, response and resolution targets, and a portal where City staff log, track and escalate requests (R118). Support covers the first 12 months after implementation at no additional charge, including month-end and year-end close assistance, and continues through annual contract renewals with the same named account manager (R114). Automated updates are applied to the hosted environment on a published schedule, and release notes and change communications are sent to City staff in advance of each update (R116). The vendor supports annual e-filing of 1099s and W-2s, including form generation, validation and submission assistance each filing season (R117). Complete support for initial implementation and for ongoing services across every application supplied is included in the subscription (R003), and dedicated technical support is staffed through implementation and each renewal (R007).

component_records.title: Pricing proposal and cost transparency
component_records.description: The price proposal is submitted on Attachment A as the cover sheet, with a detailed schedule behind it that breaks out the one-time implementation fee and the recurring annual fees separately (R090), itemizes license fees by module and by license level (R091), and identifies support service fees with implementation-period costs separated from post-implementation costs (R092). Estimated costs for any additional applications or third-party vendors needed to meet requirements are listed as a distinct line (R093). The proposal states a total price for all services and deliverables (R123), a total reimbursable expenses cap stated as a not-to-exceed figure (R124), and a total price proposal amount that is the sum of the two, so the City sees one number for the whole engagement (R125). The total cost covers all materials, supplies and travel with no uncapped reimbursables (R086, R087). The price proposal references the specific tasks and deliverables of the RFP's scope of work so each line maps to a Task 1–4 deliverable (R089).

component_records.title: Contract compliance, certifications and proposal integrity
component_records.description: The bid is submitted without any modification to the City's terms and conditions; no exceptions or alternative language are attached, and any question about terms is raised only through the RFP question process before the deadline (R024). All RFP terms are accepted as enforceable contract conditions, and the proposal acknowledges that "shall", "must" and "requirements" create binding obligations (R037, R038). A single point of contact is designated for the evaluation period, and all team members, subcontractors and suppliers are instructed in writing not to contact City staff or other parties about the proposal, on pain of disqualification (R028, R029). The price proposal is submitted final and is not revised during clarification (R031). Attachment D certifies financial condition and commits the firm to notify the City within 30 days of any change that materially alters that certification (R099), and to notify the Contract Lead within 15 days of material changes to the certification representations (R139). Attachment E provides workers compensation and commercial general liability certificates. Attachment C discloses all U.S. performance locations and states whether any work is performed outside the United States, with locations, corporate structure and a commitment to give written notice of any relocation abroad (R134). The firm bears all proposal and interview costs without reimbursement (R016).

component_records.title: Proposal administration and evaluation readiness
component_records.description: The bid team runs a submission calendar that files written questions by July 31, 2025 (R009) and holds September 25, 2025 for virtual finalist interviews if the City calls them, with the demo environment and presenters pre-booked (R011). The proposal is assembled to the RFP's structure and page limits, with the Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet completed and returned, license types by level of use described, and virtual demo availability stated. A compliance matrix maps every RFP requirement to the section of the response that answers it, so reviewers can trace coverage and the 45% goals-and-scope criterion is addressed head-on.

items.text: The City of Colfax, California, a city of just under 2,000 residents in the Sierra Nevada foothills of Placer County at the junction of Interstate 80 and State Route 174, issued this RFP on July 1, 2025.
The City operates on $6 million in annual budgeted revenues with 11 full-time employees (one position vacant) plus 1 part-time/seasonal/contract employee, and closes its fiscal year on June 30.

The City currently runs Fund Balance fund accounting software from Tyler Technologies with modules for Accounts Payable (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions, and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing, and Business Licensing, used by five users.

The City wants a streamlined package that captures financial transactions systematically and efficiently, including budgeting and forecasting, and that can generate reports and analyze data to support informed decision-making.

The City needs to maintain auditable records and documentation for future reference, and expects the vendor to understand auditing and reporting requirements and recommend an account structure for auditable reporting.

The City is replacing an existing fund accounting suite with a cloud-based system, so the bid must cover migration of existing financial, payroll, utility billing and licensing data rather than a greenfield deployment.

The City's small staff size (11 full-time employees, five software users) means the winning vendor must carry substantial implementation and training workload rather than relying on in-house City IT capacity.

The City seeks comprehensive proposals for the acquisition and implementation of a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system, including complete support for initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications the selected vendor provides.

The scope is organized into four tasks: Task 1 Approach and Project Management Plan, Task 2 Software Installation and Implementation, Task 3 Staff Training During Implementation, and Task 4 Ongoing Technical Assistance and Support.

Task 1 requires weekly progress/budget/timeline meetings, a personnel management plan with a dedicated project manager and technical staff, and a recommended account structure for auditable reporting.

Task 2 requires assistance with financial report writing, import of the prior five years of data for history, and collaboration with City Accounting and IT to minimize disruption and downtime during transition.
Task 3 requires personalized training and manuals for power users, at least one recorded training session and manual for all staff, and support for the first 12 months post-implementation.
Task 4 requires automated updates and software change communications, support for annual e-filing such as 1099s and W-2s, and a help desk or ticketing system for prioritizing support requests.
The City's goal is to go live on July 1, 2026, to align with the start of the new fiscal year, with the project starting soon after contract award and negotiation.
The City intends to award a contract to a single respondent for all items, though it reserves the right to make separate awards, not award certain items, or cancel the RFP.

Proposals are scored on four weighted criteria: 45% response to project goals and scope, 25% technical support during implementation and ongoing, 20% fee proposal and implementation schedule, and 10% information, qualifications, and references.
Written questions are due July 31, 2025, with the City's responses posted on www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025.

Proposals must be submitted by August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, with finalists notified September 11, 2025, virtual finalist interviews (if needed) on September 25, 2025, and selection and contract award on October 22, 2025.

Proposals must include a completed Attachment F Software Abilities and Requirements spreadsheet, a description of license types for different levels of use, account number customization abilities, identification of where additional applications or vendors will be used, and the availability of virtual demos.

Proposals must include an implementation plan and timeline targeting the July 1, 2026 go-live, support levels for implementation and for recurring licenses and services, key implementation personnel, training options by license level (in person, virtual, or recorded), and a client engagement approach including an account manager.
At least three references for similar services with valid e-mail addresses are required, and failure to provide a valid email may result in rejection of the proposal.
The City may select a finalist group to interview with City leadership or make a final selection without interviews, and price proposals cannot be altered or modified as part of clarification.
The City prefers at least one local referral available for an in-person software demonstration.

Proposals must not exceed 20 pages, with an additional two pages allowed for the cover letter and five pages for appendices, and must be submitted as one signed original hard copy plus one digital version.

The digital copy and all attachments must be emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov by August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST with the subject line "Accounting and Financial Software Submission", and the hard copy must arrive by the same deadline at Attn: Shanna Stahl, PO Box 702, Colfax, CA 95713 (USPS) or 33 S. Main Street, Colfax, CA 95713; late proposals will not be considered and FAX submissions are not accepted.

The City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses, so all reimbursable expenses must be capped in the Attachment A Pricing Proposal, which must state the total cost to the City for all services including materials, supplies and travel.

The price proposal must break out the implementation fee and recurring fees in detail, license fees, support service costs with implementation costs separated from post-implementation costs, and estimated costs for additional applications and/or vendors.

Respondents must submit Attachment D Certification of Financial Condition, Attachment E Certificate of Insurance covering workers compensation and commercial general liability, and Attachment G documentation of measures protecting financial data and secure access controls.
Attachment F, the Software Abilities and Requirements Excel spreadsheet, is a separate document to be provided by the City and must be completed and returned with the submission.

Attachment C requires respondents to state whether any work will be performed outside the United States, list those locations and the corporate structure of the entities performing them, identify all U.S. performance locations, and give written notice of any relocation abroad, which the City will evaluate for additional risks and costs before award.

The City rejects and will not evaluate any additional or modified terms and conditions submitted with a proposal, and objections or exceptions to the City's terms must be raised as questions under Section 2.3 during the question period or the proposal may be rejected as nonresponsive.

Respondents bear all proposal preparation and interview costs, and confidential trade secrets must be labeled "CONFIDENTIAL" at the top and bottom of each page with the specific information enclosed, while cost information cannot be marked confidential.
The City's fiscal year closes June 30, which is why the July 1, 2026 go-live is the anchor for the schedule.
The City has 11 full-time employees and five software users, so the vendor must carry most implementation workload rather than rely on City IT capacity.
The City currently runs Tyler Technologies Fund Balance modules for AP, AR, GL, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing with five users.
The City expects the vendor to understand auditing and reporting requirements and to recommend an account structure for auditable reporting.
The City is replacing an existing Tyler Technologies Fund Balance suite, so this is a migration rather than a greenfield deployment.
The City has 11 full-time employees with one position vacant, so training must be repeatable and recorded rather than one-off classroom delivery.
The City's current AP module includes 1099 filing and its payroll module implies W-2 reporting, so annual e-filing support is a continuing need.
The City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses, so every reimbursable line must carry a cap.
The City rejects and will not evaluate any additional or modified terms and conditions submitted with a proposal.
Written questions are due July 31, 2025 and finalist interviews, if needed, are scheduled for September 25, 2025.
The new system is assumed to cover all six current Fund Balance modules — AP, AR, GL, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing — with no module treated as out of scope.
Licensing is assumed to be priced for the City's current five named users with an option to add users at a published per-user rate, rather than for unlimited users.
The July 1, 2026 go-live is treated as a firm contractual milestone, with implementation assumed to begin within 30 days of the October 22, 2025 award.

The prior five years of data are assumed to be extractable from the City's existing Tyler Technologies Fund Balance system, with the vendor responsible for mapping and loading and the City responsible for confirming balances.

The 12-month post-implementation support period is assumed to be remote support during business hours with defined response targets, with on-site visits limited to the implementation and training phases.
Reimbursable expenses are assumed to be capped at a stated not-to-exceed dollar figure covering travel and materials only, with no other expense categories reimbursed.

The Attachment F and Attachment G software requirements are assumed to match the functional scope described in the RFP's scope of work, and the response is built to that scope pending the City issuing the spreadsheets.
The City's standard contract and General Contract Terms and Conditions are assumed to be acceptable as issued, since no exceptions may be filed with the proposal.
Where the certification notice periods conflict, the shorter 15-day notice to the Contract Lead is assumed to govern, with the 30-day City notice treated as satisfied by the same notification.
Insurance is assumed to be priced at commercially standard limits for a municipal software contract, with final limits confirmed when the City issues Attachment E requirements.

Attachment F and G requirements not available before the deadline. The RFP requires the Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet to be completed and returned and Attachment G documentation of data-protection measures to be submitted, but neither exhibit is in the RFP package. The bid team must price and scope against the RFP narrative alone, and any capability the spreadsheets demand beyond that narrative becomes unpriced work or a nonresponsive submission. The proposed solution assumes the attachments match the scope of work, which is an assumption the City has not confirmed. Two mandatory submission items (R101, R102) rest on documents the RFP does not include, and the solution itself records the assumption that they match the narrative scope. A mismatch would hit both responsiveness and price.

July 1, 2026 go-live treated as firm without a defined start date. The RFP states July 1, 2026 as the City's goal, not a contractual milestone, and gives no implementation start date beyond 'soon after award'. The proposed solution builds the whole schedule backwards from July 1, 2026 and assumes implementation begins within 30 days of an October 22, 2025 award. If award slips, negotiations run long, or the City later makes the date contractual, the compressed window forces parallel migration, training and cutover and risks a missed fiscal-year start. The schedule is anchored on a date the RFP calls a goal and on an award date the RFP does not guarantee; the solution's own assumption makes the date firm. A slip of a few weeks in award consumes most of the float before the June 30 fiscal close.

Standard contract and General Terms not available before the question deadline. The City's standard contract, the General Contract Terms and Conditions, and the standard City contract for services are referenced but not included, and the RFP bars any exceptions in the proposal and requires objections to be raised only during the question period. The bid team must accept unseen terms as binding, including indemnity, insurance, termination and data-ownership clauses that could materially change the risk profile or price. R024, R026, R037 and R103 make the unseen terms binding and bar exceptions in the proposal, so the only chance to object is the question window. The solution assumes the terms are acceptable, which is unverified.

Attachment E insurance requirements unknown, so insurance cannot be priced. Attachment E (certificate of insurance) is referenced but not included, and the RFP states the required coverage types only as 'including, but not limited to' with no limits, additional-insured status or certificate form. The bidder cannot confirm its current policies qualify or price any additional premium, and a limit above what the firm carries would be an unplanned cost or a responsiveness failure. R100 makes proof of insurance a mandatory submission item and the limits are unstated; the solution's assumption of 'commercially standard limits' is unverified. Municipal contracts commonly require higher limits and additional-insured endorsements.

Conflicting certification notice periods (30 days vs 15 days). R099 requires notice to the City within 30 days of any change materially altering the certification, while R139 requires notice to the Contract Lead within 15 days of the same changes. The proposed solution resolves the conflict by assuming the 15-day notice governs and satisfies both, but if the City enforces the 30-day City notice separately, a single notification to the Contract Lead could be treated as a breach of the other obligation. The two requirements are directly contradictory on both the period and the recipient, and the Contract Lead is not identified anywhere in the RFP. The solution's resolution is an assumption, not a City position.

Five years of history may not be cleanly extractable from Tyler Fund Balance. The solution commits to extracting, mapping, cleansing and loading five years of financial, payroll, utility billing and licensing history from the City's existing Tyler system, with the vendor responsible for mapping and loading. The RFP does not state the source format, data volumes or who owns cleansing, and legacy fund-accounting data is often inconsistent across years. Poor extract quality would push migration rework into the critical path before the fiscal-year cutover. R110 makes the five-year import mandatory and the solution carries the mapping and cleansing burden, but the RFP leaves the source system, volumes and cleansing responsibility open. The risk is amplified by the fixed go-live date.

Support scope for the first 12 months is undefined and may be underpriced. The solution prices 12 months of post-implementation support as remote, business-hours support with defined response targets, but the RFP does not define hours, response times, channels or on-site expectations for that period. If the City expects on-site close assistance or extended hours, the fixed fee absorbs unplanned staffing, and the 25% technical-support criterion may be scored against a level of service the bid did not describe. R114 and R118 make support mandatory but the RFP leaves service levels open, and the solution's remote-only assumption is an inference. Support is a quarter of the evaluation weight, so both price and score are exposed.

Module scope and user licensing basis not settled. The RFP lists the City's current modules but does not say whether all six must be replicated or whether Utility Billing and Business Licensing are out of scope, and it does not say whether five users is the licensed count or a floor. The solution assumes all six modules and five named users with per-user add-ons. If the City expects unlimited users or additional modules, the license and implementation price is wrong. R008 makes module coverage mandatory but the RFP never confirms the module list or user basis, and the solution's assumptions on both are inferences. Licensing drives both the recurring fee and the implementation effort.

Reimbursable expense cap has no stated ceiling or eligible categories. The RFP requires a capped reimbursable expense figure and a total price proposal that sums the service price and the cap, but gives no cap level, basis or list of eligible expenses. The solution assumes a not-to-exceed figure covering travel and materials only. If the City expects a lower cap or a broader eligible-expense list, the bid either overprices or absorbs costs it did not recover. R087, R124 and R125 make the cap mandatory and the total price depends on it, yet the RFP leaves the amount and categories open. The solution's cap is an assumption rather than a City-set figure.

Attachment A pricing form not provided, so the price format may be nonresponsive. Attachment A is required as the cover sheet for the price proposal, but the form is not in the RFP package and the required granularity of the cost breakdown is undefined. The solution builds its own detailed schedule behind Attachment A. If the City's template differs, the price submission may be rejected as nonresponsive or require rework after the deadline, when price proposals cannot be altered. R088 makes Attachment A mandatory and R031 bars price changes after submission, so a format mismatch cannot be corrected later. The RFP leaves the template and detail level open.

Small City staff may not sustain the implementation workload the plan assumes. The solution relies on City Accounting and IT as named counterparts for weekly meetings, data validation, trial-balance sign-off and training, while the City has 11 full-time employees, one vacancy and five software users. If City staff cannot keep pace with validation and cutover windows, the schedule slips against the fiscal-year deadline and the vendor absorbs rework. The RFP's own staffing figures show very limited City capacity, and the solution's plan depends on City participation at several gates. The RFP does not commit City staff time or name counterparts.

Offshoring disclosure may raise City-evaluated cost and risk. Attachment C requires the bidder to disclose any work performed outside the United States, the locations and corporate structure, and to give written notice of any relocation abroad, which the City will evaluate for additional risks and costs before award. If any delivery or support is offshore, the disclosure may reduce the score or add contractual conditions, and the notice obligation continues through the contract term. R134 and R131–R133 make disclosure mandatory and the City explicitly reserves the right to weigh it, but the RFP does not say how it scores. The impact depends on the bidder's delivery model, which the RFP does not settle.
